expectations.text: Audience characterized at a useful specificity — narrow enough that some direction shapes are clearly right and some clearly wrong
expectations.evidence: Para 1: 'manager in their first 6–18 months in the role, with multiple direct reports and a recurring 1:1 cadence already established'; rules in new-manager shapes, rules out tenured-leader shapes.

expectations.text: Current state of the landscape named — what tools or services the audience uses today, and the named ways those tools fail
expectations.evidence: Para 2 names three categories (Lighthouse/Hypercontext agenda templates; Lattice/15Five/CultureAmp/Leapsome talent suites; Apple Notes/Notion personal docs) each with their specific failure modes.

expectations.text: Real research signals only — aggregate signals, sourced findings, paraphrased user behavior; no fabricated quotes; no composite case studies with first-name attribution
expectations.evidence: Aggregate signals only; cites named frameworks (Hill, Gallup, Edmondson, MIT Sloan). No invented quotes or first-name personas.

expectations.text: Citations or (Inferred) markers on empirical claims — sources cited where claims are empirical; (Inferred) marks extensions
expectations.evidence: Linda Hill's Becoming a Manager (HBSP 2003; HBR 2007), CCL, SHRM, Gallup State of the Global Workplace, Edmondson ASQ 1999, MIT Sloan Management Review all cited; two (Inferred) markers explicitly flag extensions.

expectations.text: Source-quality hierarchy respected AND the highest-tier source available was reached for — primary government, peer-reviewed, or established non-profit sources used where they exist for this domain
expectations.evidence: Peer-reviewed (Edmondson ASQ 1999), established research orgs and academic (Hill HBSP, CCL, MIT Sloan, Gallup, SHRM, HBR). Practitioner-product mentions only as landscape, not as foundational claims.

expectations.text: Strategic, not execution — every claim passes the operational test; no rendering-layer guidance appears
expectations.evidence: All claims affect direction choice (which moment to support, audience variance, prep-stance vs topic list); no rendering or visual-design content.

expectations.text: No success criteria smuggled in — quantified targets and KPIs are absent
expectations.evidence: Gallup's 70% manager-engagement variance is a fact about the landscape, not a target for the design.

expectations.text: No direction candidates smuggled in for the design — solution-shape proposals for the design are absent; landscape players (what the audience confronts today) is fine
expectations.evidence: Strategic-positioning paragraph names the gap (prep moment, relational stance) without prescribing shape; landscape products are existing players, not design proposals.

expectations.text: No execution-layer guidance — no typography, contrast, sizing, motion, ARIA, copy-pattern specifics
expectations.evidence: No execution-layer rendering content anywhere in the doc.
Five short paragraphs (audience; landscape; behavioral/prep moment; audience variance; strategic positioning); within range.
